agencies.name: Hook Agency
agencies.tagline: Minneapolis agency focused on Google marketing (SEO, PPC and websites) for roofing, HVAC and other home-service contractors, with published starting prices
agencies.typical_retainer_usd: Published starting prices: Local SEO $2,800/mo, PPC $2,000/mo (scales with scope and ad spend), Meta ads $3,000/mo, AEO $4,000/mo ($2,000/mo added to an SEO package); websites $12,000 (standard) or $24,000 (custom) split over 12 months, complex sites up to $50,000
agencies.long_description:
Hook Agency is a Minneapolis digital marketing agency for home-service contractors, led by founder and CEO Tim Brown and co-owner Bea Bonte. Hook's own company history says Tim launched the business as "Tim B Design" in 2016, made the first hires under the Hook Agency name in 2017-2018, chose to work only with roofing and home-services clients in 2021, and has since expanded from roofing into HVAC. Hook describes a team of 30+ people and says it has served 200+ contractors.

Hook says it concentrates on Google marketing: local SEO, AEO (optimization for AI-driven search results), pay-per-click including Google Ads and Local Services Ads, and website design. Its homepage lists roofing, HVAC and plumbing among the trades it serves. Its homepage FAQ also lists Google Business Profile management and Meta ads, which Hook says it builds on real video of your team, shot by a videographer it sends to your office or jobsite at no extra cost; its pricing page lists Meta ads from $3,000/mo. Organic social media management is not on its service list. Hook says content writing is built into its SEO work rather than sold as a separate service.

Hook publishes starting prices on its pricing page: Local SEO from $2,800/mo, PPC from $2,000/mo (scaling with scope and ad spend), Meta ads from $3,000/mo, and AEO at $4,000/mo, or $2,000/mo when added to an SEO package. A standard website is $12,000 and a custom website $24,000, each split into 12 monthly payments, and Hook says more complex sites can cost up to $50,000. Services are priced separately, so a program that combines SEO, PPC and a website costs the sum. Hook's FAQ says it asks for a yearly commitment.

Hook also publishes a large amount of free material for contractors: a blog, a YouTube channel and roofing and HVAC podcasts. That lets you judge its thinking before a sales call, but read it as the vendor's own marketing.

The trade-off: Hook's published prices make budgeting easier, but they are per service and stack, every engagement starts with a yearly commitment, and the focus is Google channels for home-service contractors plus Meta ads, rather than a full-service mix that includes organic social media management.
agencies.how_it_works: Book a call through Hook Agency's website. Hook reviews your business and market and proposes a scope. Published starting prices: Local SEO $2,800/mo, PPC $2,000/mo (scales with scope and ad spend), Meta ads $3,000/mo, AEO $4,000/mo ($2,000/mo when added to an SEO package), and websites at $12,000 (standard) or $24,000 (custom), split over 12 months. Hook asks for a yearly commitment. Its pricing page says SEO clients get monthly reporting dashboards and video calls.

pros_detail.explanation: Hook publishes a blog, a YouTube channel and roofing and HVAC podcasts, so you can judge its approach before you talk to sales.

pros_detail.explanation: Standard ($12,000) and custom ($24,000) websites are split into 12 monthly payments of $1,000 or $2,000, according to the pricing page.

cons_detail.explanation: Each service has its own starting price (for example $2,800/mo for local SEO plus $2,000/mo for PPC), and PPC scales with scope and ad spend, so a multi-channel program costs well above any single figure.

cons_detail.explanation: Hook's FAQ says it asks for a yearly commitment, so plan on a 12-month engagement from the start.

cons_detail.explanation: Hook's services center on Google channels (SEO, Google Ads, Local Services Ads, Google Business Profile, websites) plus AEO and Meta ads; organic social media management is not on its service list, so confirm what is included if you need it.

cons_detail.explanation: Hook says more complex websites can cost up to $50,000, well above the published $24,000 custom tier.

agency_faqs.a: Hook publishes starting prices: Local SEO $2,800/mo, PPC $2,000/mo (scaling with scope and ad spend), Meta ads $3,000/mo, and AEO $4,000/mo ($2,000/mo when added to SEO). agencies.name: Plumbing & HVAC SEO
agencies.tagline: Doral, Florida marketing agency for plumbing, HVAC and electrical contractors, with a published $2,495/month core program
agencies.typical_retainer_usd: $2,495/mo core program (one trade, one location) + $5,000 one-time setup; add-ons from $395/mo; the company says most clients invest $3,500-$5,000+/mo
agencies.long_description:
Plumbing & HVAC SEO is a digital marketing agency for plumbing, HVAC and electrical contractors, founded by Josh Nelson (co-founder and CEO) and Dean Iodice (founder and president). Its website footer describes it as "A Clic Inc. Company," and Josh Nelson's own site says his earlier general marketing agency narrowed its focus to plumbing and HVAC in 2011. The company lists its office in Doral, Florida, says it has served 600+ contractors with clients in the US, Canada and Australia, and Josh Nelson's site describes a 35-person team.

The pricing page lists a core program at $2,495/month covering one trade, one location, one primary city and ten surrounding cities, plus a one-time $5,000 setup fee for competitive research, tooling, hosting and the website build. The core program includes a conversion-focused website, SEO (which the company calls Search Everywhere Optimization), monthly content, competitive analysis, reputation management, NAP (name, address, phone) cleanup, marketing automation, three hours a month of website changes, and KPI reporting with monthly strategy calls.

Add-ons are priced on the same page: Google Ads management at $1,500/month for up to $10,000 in ad spend, then 15% of spend above that; Local Services Ads management at $549/month up to 75 calls, $949 up to 150 and $1,549 up to 200; Meta advertising at $750/month; $750/month for each additional trade; $500/month for each additional location or Google Business Profile; $500/month per ten additional cities; and advanced ROI reporting at $395/month. The company says most clients invest $3,500 to $5,000+ per month.

The agreement starts with a twelve-month initial term, then runs month-to-month with thirty days' notice to cancel, and the pricing page says ownership of the website is released to you free after twelve months. Josh Nelson's site says Plumbing & HVAC SEO has made the Inc. 5000 list of fast-growing private companies three times.

The trade-off: the pricing and the contents of the core program are spelled out, but the core fee covers one trade and one location, the $5,000 setup and add-ons raise the cost quickly, and you commit for twelve months before month-to-month terms apply.
agencies.how_it_works: Start with a call about your business, service area and current marketing. The core program is $2,495/month (one trade, one location, one primary city plus ten surrounding cities) with a $5,000 one-time setup that covers research, tooling, hosting and the website build. Add-ons include Google Ads management ($1,500/month up to $10,000 in ad spend, then 15% above), Local Services Ads ($549-$1,549/month by call volume), Meta ads ($750/month), extra trades ($750/month each), extra locations ($500/month each) and advanced ROI reporting ($395/month). Reporting includes KPIs and monthly strategy calls. Twelve-month initial term, then month-to-month with 30 days' notice.

cons_detail.explanation: Roofing, landscaping and other trades are outside its focus, so contractors in those trades should look at other agencies.

agency_faqs.a: Different focus. Plumbing & HVAC SEO markets to plumbing, HVAC and electrical contractors; Hook Agency centers on roofing and HVAC. agencies.name: Blue Corona (merged into RYNO Strategic Solutions, an EverService Holdings company)
agencies.tagline: Home-services digital marketing agency, founded in 2007, that merged into RYNO Strategic Solutions on October 1, 2024 and now operates under the RYNO brand
agencies.typical_retainer_usd: Not published; quoted by RYNO Strategic Solutions
agencies.long_description:
Blue Corona is a digital marketing agency for home-service businesses. Its about page says it was founded in 2007 by Ben Landers with the help of Bob Perini, and its site lists an office in Gaithersburg, Maryland. EverService, a provider of tech-enabled business services, acquired Blue Corona in November 2022 and acquired RYNO Strategic Solutions in May 2023.

Effective October 1, 2024, Blue Corona and RYNO Strategic Solutions merged and now operate under the RYNO Strategic Solutions brand. The merger announcement says RYNO is a wholly owned subsidiary of EverService Holdings, LLC, a portfolio company of the growth equity firm Sunstone Partners, and that Mike Wilson is CEO of both RYNO and EverService Holdings. The bluecorona.com site still loads, but it carries a merger banner and a "Blue Corona Is Now RYNO" link to rynoss.com.

The bluecorona.com site lists website design and development, SEO, PPC, Google Local Services Ads, email marketing, social media marketing, OTT (streaming TV) advertising, live lead capture, chat, lead recovery, and tracking and reporting. Its industry list includes HVAC, plumbing, electrical, pest control, roofing, remodeling, garage doors, landscaping, painting, moving, solar, windows and doors, flooring, home builders and franchises.

Neither bluecorona.com nor the merger announcement publishes retainer prices or contract terms, so price and minimum commitment are quoted by RYNO. Because Blue Corona now operates as RYNO (profiled separately in this directory), evaluate RYNO's current team, services and terms directly.

The trade-off: the combined agency lists a broad multi-channel service menu across many home-service trades, but you are buying from RYNO under EverService's ownership, and you need a quote to learn the price and contract length.
agencies.how_it_works: Contact RYNO Strategic Solutions (bluecorona.com links visitors to rynoss.com) to discuss your business and marketing needs. RYNO proposes a scope from its service list, which on bluecorona.com includes websites, SEO, PPC, Local Services Ads, email, social media, OTT advertising, lead capture and reporting. Retainer pricing and contract length are quoted; neither Blue Corona's site nor the merger announcement publishes them.

pros_detail.explanation: The site lists websites, SEO, PPC, Local Services Ads, email, social media, OTT advertising, live lead capture, chat and reporting.

pros_detail.title: Long operating history (since 2007)
pros_detail.explanation: Blue Corona's about page says it was founded in 2007; that history now sits inside RYNO.

pros_detail.title: Wide trade coverage
pros_detail.explanation: The site lists more than a dozen home-service industries, from HVAC and plumbing to pest control, moving and solar.

cons_detail.title: Now operates as RYNO
cons_detail.explanation: Blue Corona merged into RYNO Strategic Solutions effective October 1, 2024 and unified under the RYNO brand, so the Blue Corona name no longer describes an independent agency. Evaluate RYNO's current team, terms and reporting rather than Blue Corona's pre-merger track record.

cons_detail.title: No published pricing or terms
cons_detail.explanation: Neither bluecorona.com nor the merger announcement lists retainer prices or contract length, so you must request a quote.

cons_detail.title: Part of a larger holding company
cons_detail.explanation: RYNO is a subsidiary of EverService Holdings, which is backed by Sunstone Partners and bought Blue Corona in 2022 and RYNO in 2023; ask who will manage your account day to day.

agencies.best_for: Home-service contractors who want one agency to run several channels (website, SEO, PPC, email, social) and are willing to evaluate RYNO, which Blue Corona merged into in October 2024
agencies.best_team_size: Home-service businesses with budget for a multi-channel retainer; pricing is quoted
agencies.weaknesses: Blue Corona no longer operates independently (it is now RYNO), and pricing and contract terms are not published
agencies.affiliate_payout_note: No editorial affiliate program

agency_faqs.q: Should I work with Blue Corona or a trade-specific specialist?
agency_faqs.a: Blue Corona is now part of RYNO, so the comparison is RYNO against a specialist. RYNO offers a broad multi-channel service menu across many home-service trades; specialists such as Hook Agency (roofing and HVAC) and Plumbing & HVAC SEO (plumbing, HVAC and electrical) focus on fewer trades and publish their pricing.

agency_faqs.q: Is Blue Corona still an independent agency?
agency_faqs.a: No. Blue Corona and RYNO Strategic Solutions merged effective October 1, 2024, unifying under the RYNO brand, and bluecorona.com now points visitors to RYNO. RYNO is a wholly owned subsidiary of EverService Holdings, LLC, a portfolio company of Sunstone Partners. EverService had acquired Blue Corona in November 2022.

agencies.name: Adapt Digital Solutions
agencies.tagline: Coeur d'Alene, Idaho agency founded by a former contractor, offering Google-focused marketing (websites, SEO, Local Services Ads, Google Ads) month to month
agencies.typical_retainer_usd: Not published (quoted after a call); month-to-month, no long-term contracts
agencies.long_description:
Adapt Digital Solutions (styled ADAPT) is a small marketing agency for contractors and other local service businesses, founded by Chuck Kile, whom the company describes as a life-long contractor. Its about page is titled "Contractor Marketing Since 2018," and its homepage lists its headquarters in Coeur d'Alene, Idaho. Chuck says he turned to marketing while working as a superintendent at a Portland remodeling company that suddenly had no jobs in the pipeline. The about page introduces a small team that includes an SEO manager, an ads manager and a webmaster.

Adapt says it concentrates on Google marketing, organized as four layers: a foundation of a website and Google Business Profile, local SEO, Google Local Services Ads, and Google Ads. Its services page also lists ChatGPT ads, audits and consultations, website maintenance and CRM integration, and the site has a print marketing page. Adapt says it serves contractors of all trades (remodelers, plumbers, HVAC, electricians, roofers, landscapers and painters), groundwater companies, IT service providers and other local service businesses such as cleaning and pest control.

Adapt does not publish prices; pricing is discussed after you contact the team. The homepage says clients use Adapt as their marketing department month to month with no long-term contracts required, and the website maintenance page describes that plan as month-to-month, cancel anytime. The about page says the team has built websites for more than 400 construction companies and that roughly 150 companies use its ongoing marketing each month.

Adapt publishes a large library of free articles on contractor marketing and lead generation, including guides to Google Local Services Ads and state-by-state contractor licensing, and Chuck runs a YouTube channel, "Chuck the Contractor," which the site says has 20K+ subscribers.

The trade-off: Adapt offers month-to-month terms and a founder with contracting experience, but it is a small team, it publishes no prices, and its service list centers on Google channels rather than social media.
agencies.how_it_works: Contact Adapt through its website form to talk about your business. Adapt offers an audit and consultation, then proposes work from its four layers: website and Google Business Profile, local SEO, Local Services Ads and Google Ads. Prices are quoted, not published. Monthly marketing runs month-to-month with no long-term contract, according to the homepage.

agencies.name: Lemonade Stand
agencies.tagline: Orem, Utah full-service digital marketing agency with home-services specialty pages, no contracts and no setup fees
agencies.typical_retainer_usd: Not published (quote on request); no contracts, no setup fees
agencies.long_description:
Lemonade Stand is a full-service digital marketing agency in Orem, Utah. Its company page says it has helped build, grow and measure the online presence of thousands of businesses since 2012, and that it also created Yalla, a team management and collaboration platform. It describes itself as a Google Partner and Bing Ads Accredited Professional.

Lemonade Stand is not a trade-only agency. Its specialty pages cover law firms, auto body shops, medical providers, managed IT providers, e-commerce and self-storage as well as home services. Its home-services page names plumbing, HVAC, landscaping, pest control, electricians, solar and roofing, and it has separate pages for HVAC, plumbers, pest control and pool contractors.

Services listed on the site include SEO, optimization for AI search, PPC, social media marketing and paid social ads, content writing, backlink outreach, YouTube ads, retargeting, reputation management, website design, video and podcast production, graphic design, an outsourced CMO service and performance-based PR. For home-services companies it also lists Google Local Services Ads management.

Lemonade Stand does not publish prices; you request a quote. The company says it has no contracts and no setup fees and describes its management fees as transparent. Its home-services page features a case study of RighTime Home Services.

The trade-off: no contracts and no setup fees lower the risk of trying Lemonade Stand, but it serves many industries rather than only trades, and you need a quote to learn the monthly cost.

Lemonade Stand says it has no contracts and no setup fees, so the engagement continues only as long as you keep paying month to month.

agencies.name: Builder Funnel
agencies.tagline: Fully remote marketing agency, headquartered in Colorado Springs, that works only with residential remodelers and custom home builders and publishes its pricing
agencies.typical_retainer_usd: $3,500-$7,500/mo (Build $3,500, Growth $5,000, Accelerate $7,500) after a UDMS setup package (Build $15,000, $5,000/mo over 3 months; Showcase $25,500, $8,500/mo over 3 months); technology from $540/mo; add-ons $300-$750; ad spend separate (suggested $1,000-$5,000/mo)
agencies.long_description:
Builder Funnel is a marketing agency that says it works exclusively with residential remodelers and custom home builders. Founder and CEO Spencer Powell started it in 2010 as a one-person operation inside his family's direct-mail business. Its about page now describes a fully remote, 40+ person agency serving builders and remodelers across the country, lists its headquarters in Colorado Springs, Colorado, and says it has 84 clients. Builder Funnel says it made the Inc. 5000 list in 2024 and 2025 and is a HubSpot Diamond Partner.

Because it serves only remodelers and custom home builders, Builder Funnel is not an option for service trades such as HVAC, plumbing, electrical or roofing service work; its own FAQ says it does not work with businesses outside remodeling and custom homes.

Builder Funnel publishes its pricing as three steps. First comes a setup package it calls the Ultimate Digital Marketing System (UDMS): Build at $15,000 ($5,000 a month over three months), covering website design and development, SEO setup, lead generation, a CRM, tracking, email marketing, a social media audit and a marketing plan; or Showcase at $25,500 ($8,500 a month over three months), which adds an on-site filming trip, long-form videos, Instagram Reels, drone footage and B-roll. Second comes a monthly plan: Build at $3,500, Growth at $5,000 or Accelerate at $7,500, which differ in content pieces, social posts, emails, lead generation campaigns and how much ad spend they manage (up to $5,000, $10,000 or $25,000). Third are add-ons from $300/month (Email Booster) to $750 (per SEO and AI content piece, or per month for the Social Booster).

Technology and ad spend are separate from the retainer: technology starts at $540/month, and suggested ad spend ranges from $1,000/month on Build to $5,000/month on Accelerate. Builder Funnel's FAQ says a website needs an ongoing retainer to generate leads and suggests budgeting 3-5% of your revenue goal each year for all marketing. The pricing page does not state a minimum contract length.

The trade-off: Builder Funnel's pricing is published and its focus on remodelers and custom builders is clear, but the first-year cost is high once setup, retainer, technology and ad spend are added together, and service-trade contractors fall outside its market.
agencies.how_it_works: Schedule a consultation, where Builder Funnel reviews your revenue, goals and current marketing. The published process starts with a UDMS setup package (Build $15,000 or Showcase $25,500, each paid over three months), then a monthly plan of $3,500, $5,000 or $7,500, plus technology from $540/month and separate ad spend. Add-ons run $300-$750. The pricing page does not publish a minimum contract length.

pros_detail.explanation: Builder Funnel says it works exclusively with residential remodelers and custom home builders, so its team markets only that kind of business.

pros_detail.title: Published pricing
pros_detail.explanation: Setup packages, monthly plans, add-ons, the technology fee and suggested ad spend are all listed on the pricing page.

pros_detail.title: Long track record
pros_detail.explanation: Builder Funnel was founded in 2010, and its about page says it has 84 clients and made the Inc. 5000 list in 2024 and 2025.

cons_detail.title: Not for service trades
